ma.quote: Msumbiji This site consists of a small primary reef with a variety of soft and hard corals on slopes and sheer walls down to 15 m.

tm.quote: Msumbiji: This site consists of a small primary reef with a variety of soft and hard corals on slopes and sheer walls down to 15 m.

summary.text: A compact reef with soft and hard corals on slopes and short walls, plus coral spires with archways and overhangs away from the main formation. Visibility can be unpredictable.

tgi.quote: Mwana Wa Mwana Dive Type: Coral garden Depth: 3-12 m, 12-18 m Mwana Wa Mwana is a brilliant dive site for snorkelers, beginner and qualified divers

zw.quote: Mwana na Mwana (2-12m): Soft and hard coral bommies with glass fish sheltering in the crevices. Frogfish have been spotted here

oo5.quote: The Great Northern Level: beginner Depth: 4-12 m A British cable-laying ship, The Great Northern was built in 1870 and sank on New Year’s Eve in 1902. She now rests in the sand between 4 and 12 m and is a magnificent artificial reef.
Bawe Reef Level: beginner-intermediate Depth: 5-18 m The island Bawe just off the coast of Stone Town, is our go-to reef.

Bawe Reef Level: beginner-intermediate Depth: 5-18 m The island Bawe just off the coast of Stone Town, is our go-to reef. We have 3 dive sites around the island. One is on the North side and is a continuous coral wall teeming with life.

tgi.quote: Ras Misikitini Dive Type: Small wall Depth: 5-12 m, 12-20 m Ras Misikitini is an impressive dive site for snorkelers, beginner and qualified divers

zw.quote: Tumbatu – Haunted wall (2-15m): A small eerie looking wall with beautiful soft corals sheltering nudibranchs and leaf fish, with inquisitive bat fish cruising past.

highlights.text: Soft corals with nudibranchs, leaf fish, batfish

tgi.quote: Shetani Dive Type: Small wall Depth: 3-16 m Shetani is a vibrant dive site for snorkelers, beginner and qualified divers
Shane’s Reef Dive Type: Coral reef Depth: 10-20 m Shane´s Reef is a unique dive site for beginner and qualified divers

zw.quote: Shanes Reef (12-16m): This weird and wonderful dive offers the best array of macro life around. Flying gurnards frogfish and Mauritius scorpion fish make this site a photographers dream.

highlights.text: Macro life: flying gurnards, frogfish, scorpionfish

summary.text: A sand-and-coral reef off northern Zanzibar prized for macro photography, with frogfish, gurnards and scorpionfish. Depths stay moderate, so it works for newer divers.

tgi.quote: Mbwangawa Dive Type: Coral reef Depth: 7-18 m Mbwangawa is a relaxing dive site for both the experienced and inexperienced divers

zw.quote: Mbwangawa (12-18m): An eclectic mix of life, including lobster sheltering beneath plate corals and frequent encounters with cuttlefish.

highlights.text: Lobsters under plate corals, cuttlefish, turtles

summary.text: An extensive reef of hard and soft corals with plate-coral patches off northeast Zanzibar. A mild current allows a relaxed drift, with lobsters, cuttlefish and turtles regularly seen.

tgi.quote: Kichafi Dive Type: Coral reef Depth: 10-16 m Kichafi is an amazing reef for both the experienced and inexperienced divers

zw.quote: Kichafi (12-18m): A very healthy reef with vast expanses of plate corals.

highlights.text: Healthy reef with extensive plate corals

summary.text: A healthy coral reef with broad plate-coral fields, suited to mixed-experience groups. A sandy area next to the reef makes it popular for training dives.

zw.quote: Renco Bommi (7-14m): A huge coral bommi coming up from the sand, with an explosion of marine life. Leaf fish, Octopus, and the colorful Mantis shrimps are a common site here. An ideal dive site for the less experienced.
Haji (10-18m): A submerged coral ridge attracts an abundance of marine life and sports a vast array of hard coral formations. There are numerous Crocodile fish and Nudibranchs to be found here.

tgi.quote: Hunga Reef Dive Type: Coral bommies Depth: 10-17 m Hunga Reef is a stunning dive site for qualified divers

ts.quote: Hunga Reef Located underneath Shane’s Reef and to the northwest of Zanzibar, this circular reef is another that is found in the open sea with a depth of 10 to 17 meters. Hunga is known for its excellent level of visibility

summary.text: A circular open-sea reef with big coral bommies off northwest Zanzibar, known for clear water. Aimed at certified divers rather than first-timers.
